## Week 1 Exercises

Exercise 1.3.

First need to install the package ISLR2 and call the library.

```{r}
# import relevant packages
library(ISLR2)
library(glmnet)
library(lars)
library(remotes)
library(HDeconometrics)
library(leaps)
ds <- data(Hitters)

```

Check for missing data like in Section 6.5 of ISL book

```{r}
# see we have 59 missing data points
sum(is.na(Hitters$Salary))

# transform the data to have the data without the NA data-points
Hitters <- na.omit(Hitters)

x <- model.matrix(Salary~ ., Hitters)[, -1]

y <- Hitters$Salary
```

# first try

```{r}
set.seed(333)
train <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), nrow(Hitters),
replace = TRUE)
test <- (!train)

regfit.best <- regsubsets(Salary ~ ., data = Hitters[train, ], nvmax = 19)

test.mat <- model.matrix(Salary ~ ., data = Hitters[test, ])
val.errors <- rep(NA, 19)

for (i in 1:19) {
  coefi <- coef(regfit.best, id = i)
  pred <- test.mat[, names(coefi)] %*% coefi
  val.errors[i] <- mean((Hitters$Salary[test] - pred)^2)
}

which.min(val.errors)

train <- sample(1:nrow(x), nrow(x) / 2)
test <- (-train)
y.test <- y[test]

predict.regsubsets <- function(object, newdata , id, ...) {
 form <- as.formula(object$call[[2]])
 mat <- model.matrix(form, newdata)
 coefi <- coef(object, id = id)
 xvars <- names(coefi)
 mat[, xvars] %*% coefi
}

regfit.best <- regsubsets(Salary ~ ., data = Hitters, nvmax = 19)
coef(regfit.best, 13)
 
k <- 10
n <- nrow(Hitters)
set.seed(1)
folds <- sample(rep(1:k, length = n))
cv.errors <- matrix(NA, k, 19,
dimnames = list(NULL, paste(1:19)))

for (j in 1:k) {
  best.fit <- regsubsets(Salary ~ .,
  data = Hitters[folds != j, ],
  nvmax = 19)
  for (i in 1:19) {
    pred <- predict(best.fit, Hitters[folds == j, ], id = i)
    cv.errors[j, i] <-
    mean((Hitters$Salary[folds == j] - pred)^2)
  }
}

mean.cv.errors <- apply(cv.errors, 2, mean)
mean.cv.errors

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
plot(mean.cv.errors, type = "b")

reg.best <- regsubsets(Salary ~ ., data = Hitters,
nvmax = 19)
coef(reg.best, 10)



```

# second try

Use the cv. for cross validation to make it shorter.

```{r}
# initialise the situation again in case something was done wrong in the first try
set.seed(333)

Hitters <- na.omit(Hitters)

x <- model.matrix(Salary~ ., Hitters)[, -1]
y <- Hitters$Salary

# make grid and train + test sets again
grid <- 10^seq(10, -2, length = 100)
train <- sample(1:nrow(x), nrow(x) / 2)
test <- (-train)
y.test <- y[test]

# fit the lasso on the training data using the grid
lasso.mod <- glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 1, lambda = grid)

# cross validate to find best lambda
cv.out.lasso <- cv.glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 1)
bestlam.lasso <- cv.out.lasso$lambda.min

# now check the performance 
lasso.pred <- predict(lasso.mod, s = bestlam.lasso, newx = x[test, ])
lasso.mse <- mean((lasso.pred - y.test)^2)
print(paste("Lasso Test MSE:", lasso.mse))

# refit on the actual sample to find the zero and non zero coefficients
out.lasso <- glmnet(x, y, alpha = 1, lambda = grid)
lasso.coef <- predict(out.lasso, type = "coefficients", s = bestlam.lasso)[1:20, ]
lasso.coef

```
Now we want to look how the ridge, elastic net, and adaptive lasso compare to this.
To see this we have to perform the same things on those aapproaches.

```{r}
# for ridge need alpha = 0
ridge.mod <- glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 0, lambda = grid)

# cross validate and estimate best lambda
cv.out.ridge <- cv.glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 0)
bestlam.ridge <- cv.out.ridge$lambda.min

# predict on the test set and see how it performs
ridge.pred <- predict(ridge.mod, s = bestlam.ridge, newx = x[test, ])
ridge.mse <- mean((ridge.pred - y.test)^2)
print(paste("Ridge Test MSE:", ridge.mse))

coef(ridge.mod)[, 50]

```

Now do the elastic net.

```{r}
# for the elastic net set alpha = 0.5
elastic.mod <- glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 0.5, lambda = grid)

# cross validate on training set and find best lambda
cv.out.elastic <- cv.glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 0.5)
bestlam.elastic <- cv.out.elastic$lambda.min

# check how it performs versus testing set
elastic.pred <- predict(elastic.mod, s = bestlam.elastic, newx = x[test, ])
elastic.mse <- mean((elastic.pred - y.test)^2)
print(paste("Elastic Net Test MSE:", elastic.mse))

coef(elastic.mod)[,80]

```
 
Finally, check adaptive lasso. Need to do an initial estimation to find coefficients for the weights. We have a 250 observation and 19 feautures/variables, so we can use OLS to find the initial estimation.

```{r}
# so, we want to fit an ols on the training data
# transform data so that it can take the lm() function
olsdata <- data.frame(y = y[train], x[train, ])
fitols <- lm(y ~ ., data = olsdata)

# then we take the coefficients (other than the intercept as was mentioned in the slides)
coefols <- coef(fitols)[-1]

# we then make these into the weights like in the slides by dividing 1 with them
weightols <- 1 / (abs(coefols) + 1e-7) # added 1e-7 since i got a divide by zero error

# then we fit the adaptive lasso using the same glmnet as for lasso, but with the given weights
cv.adapt <- cv.glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 1, penalty.factor = weightols)
bestlam.adapt <- cv.adapt$lambda.min

# finally, we check the performance on the test set
adapt.pred <- predict(cv.adapt, s = bestlam.adapt, newx = x[test, ])
adapt.mse <- mean((adapt.pred - y.test)^2)
print(paste("Adaptive Lasso Test MSE:", adapt.mse))

coef(ridge.mod)[, 50]

```
Now we have to use information criteria (aic and bic) to find lambda and compare with what we found previously. We will use the ic.glmnet functions from HDeconometrics.
So, just run lasso and use this function to find aic and bic.

```{r}
# fit the lasso and find ic in one go
# first aic
iclasso <- ic.glmnet(x, y, alpha = 1, crit = "aic")

# Extract non-zero coefficients for AIC
aiccoef <- iclasso$coef
aiccoef

# now bic
iclasso <- ic.glmnet(x, y, alpha = 1, crit = "bic")

# Extract non-zero coefficients for BIC
biccoef <- iclasso$coef
biccoef


```

Now look at how well we predict the salaries of new players. We have the MSE for all of the previous ones, now we do the prediction for aic and bic, then compare them all.

```{r}
# aic and bic on training set 
bicfit <- ic.glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 1, crit = "bic")
aicfit <- ic.glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 1, crit = "aic")

# do the predictions
predbic <- predict(bicfit, newdata = x[test, ])
predaic <- predict(aicfit, newdata = x[test, ])

# calculate the mse for both 
bicmse <- mean((predbic - y.test)^2)
aicmse <- mean((predaic - y.test)^2)

print(paste("BIC Test MSE:", bicmse))
print(paste("CV Test MSE:", aicmse))
```
Plot them to visualise:

```{r}
msevals <- c(ridge.mse, elastic.mse, lasso.mse, adapt.mse, aicmse, bicmse)
estimators <- c("ridge", "elastic", "lasso", "adap lasso", "aic lasso", "bic lasso")

par(mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
bp <- barplot(msevals, 
              names.arg = estimators, 
              col = c("blue", "lightblue", "green", "red", "orange", "purple"),
              ylab = "test mean squared error values",
              main = "test mse comparison",
              xpd = FALSE) # xpd=FALSE clips the bars to the ylim
```
